Edit: Downvoat away! No desire to put up a fight? As of yet, no refutation of DVB being a means of censorship.

By brigade, I do not not necessarily mean a organized/coordinated group of people (though it may be), but more likely random people deliberately going through a user's comment history to downvoat everything they have said, whether or not it is relevant to the original point of contention.

Disliking another user's opinions is NOT a valid justification for duct-taping their mouths shut and oppressing their right to free speech. If you are a DV brigader who intends to put a user below -50 CCP you are nothing but a cheap and cowardly tyrant - that is what your analogue would be IRL.

A DV brigade is not the same as an UV brigade because the former will effectively SILENCE the user. The latter can indeed be abused to increase points unfairly for someone. In a case where a user has been silenced, I argue that an UV brigade can neutralize the DV brigade.

A DV brigade can have clear, negative consequences if severe enough, but an UV brigade will, at most, give someone the power to talk freely again or give someone the ability to downvoat (>100 CCP).
Dear Voaters, Advocates of Anti-Censorship - Why is a deliberate DownVoat brigade not a form of censorship?
What if the votes are organic and you are wrong? Why did you appoint yourself judge and jury of voat to decide who will get to say unpopular opinions or not?

A vote brigade is no more a censorship tool than a boycott is to a business or organization. If we as a society can support the use of boycotts to send a message that we do not agree with a company's practices or motivations then we can uphold that at an individual level as well. Many people call the downvote button a "disagree" button so an organized mass disagreement is a tool to send a message that your opinion or commentary is not popular. Companies who are boycotted are capable of suffering financial harm and have to publicly respond to save their reputations and financial standing even if it means going against their motives and agendas. A personal boycott in the form of a brigade does not usually constitute financial damages and hurts only your internet reputation (which has no arguable tangible value). You don't have to publicly apologize or change your ways after being brigaded. Individuals fare better than companies since the latter actually faces a form of censorship to save their financial skins and the former just ends up with a bruised ego. While it may not be in good taste to organize or participate in a downvote brigade, I respect the rights and privileges that allow others and myself to engage in them if inclined to do so. People have a right to speak, but people don't have a right to listened to.
